South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and ongoing management of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment one month after his last visit. He reports that while his dyspnea has remained stable, he continues to experience significant limitations during physical activity. He states that he has been using his albuterol inhaler approximately five to seven times daily, which indicates a slight improvement in his respiratory control since his last visit. He remains compliant with his inhaled corticosteroids and has been attending pulmonary rehabilitation sessions regularly.
Despite these positive changes in his respiratory management, Mr. Fairfax's bilateral lower extremity edema has shown minimal improvement. He continues to adhere to a low-sodium diet and is taking furosemide 100 mg daily. The edema is still described as 1+ pitting, and he notes that it has not worsened but has not resolved either. He continues to elevate his legs as recommended.
Mr. Fairfax expresses ongoing fatigue, which he describes as debilitating, although he reports a slight improvement in his mood and anxiety levels. He attributes this to his increased therapy sessions with a psychologist and the ongoing support from his family. He has been compliant with his sertraline regimen and feels that it has contributed positively to his emotional well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, reduced use to five to seven times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.4F, HR 76, BP 128/78, RR 20, O2 sat 87% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and mildly anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.2, Hgb 10.8, Hct 32.5, Plt 220 2. BMP: Na 136, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 23, BUN 28, Cr 1.4, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 580 (notable decrease). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's dyspnea remains stable, and he is encouraged to continue pulmonary rehabilitation and adherence to inhaled corticosteroids. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema continues to be managed with furosemide. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Mr. Fairfax has reported improvements in anxiety and depressive symptoms, and ongoing psychological support is encouraged. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
